035/**
036 * Formats a log event using a {@link StringBuilder}. <strong>All formatters should be
037 * thread-safe!</strong>.
038 * <p>
039 * The appender will make sure the {@link StringBuilder} is not shared with multiple
040 * threads so the formatter does not have to synchronize/lock on and should definitely not
041 * do that.
042 * <p>
043 * Because of various invariants the preferred way to compose formatters is to use the
044 * {@linkplain #builder() builder} which will do some optimization like combining static
045 * formatters etc.
046 *
047 * @see #builder()
048 * @see LogFormatter.EventFormatter
049 * @see LogEncoder#of(LogFormatter)
050 * @apiNote This class is sealed. An interface that has the same contract that can be
051 * implemented is {@link EventFormatter}.
052 */
053public sealed interface LogFormatter {
054
055        /**
056         * Formats a log event.
057         * @param output buffer.
058         * @param event log event.
059         * @see EventFormatter
060         */
061        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event);
062
063        /**
064         * See {@link EventFormatter#builder()}.
065         * @return builder.
066         */
067        public static Builder builder() {
068                return new Builder();
069        }
070
071        /**
072         * Create a formatter using event formatter that is a lambda so that
073         * {@code LogFormater.of((o, e) -> ...); } works.
074         * @param e will be returned.
075         * @return passed in formatter.
076         * @apiNote this is for ergonomics because LogFormatter is sealed.
077         */
078        public static EventFormatter of(EventFormatter e) {
079                return e;
080        }
081
082        /**
083         * Ask the formatter if will do anything.
084         * @return true if promises not to write to builder.
085         * @see #noop()
086         */
087        default boolean isNoop() {
088                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE == this;
089        }
090
091        /**
092         * A special formatter that will do nothing. It is a singleton so identity comparison
093         * can be used.
094         * @return a formatter that implements all formatting interfaces but does nothing.
095         */
096        public static NoopFormatter noop() {
097                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE;
098        }
099
100        /**
101         * A special formatter that will append static text.
102         *
103         * @param content static text.
104         */
105        public record StaticFormatter(String content) implements LogFormatter {
106                @Override
107                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
108                        output.append(content);
109                }
110
111                /**
112                 * Creates a new formatter by concat the {@link #content()}. This is mainly used
113                 * by the {@link EventFormatter#builder()} to coalesce multiple static text.
114                 * @param next the text that will follow this formatter.
115                 * @return new formatter.
116                 */
117                public StaticFormatter concat(StaticFormatter next) {
118                        return new StaticFormatter(this.content + next.content);
119                }
120
121                /**
122                 * Coalesce formatters that can be such as {@link StaticFormatter}.
123                 * @param formatters list of formatters in the order of which they will be
124                 * executed.
125                 * @return an array of formatters where static formatters next to each other will
126                 * be coalesced.
127                 */
128                private static LogFormatter[] coalesce(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
129                        var flattened = CompositeFormatter.flatten(formatters);
130                        List<LogFormatter> resolved = new ArrayList<>();
131                        StaticFormatter current = null;
132                        for (var f : flattened) {
133                                if (f.isNoop()) {
134                                }
135                                else if (current == null && f instanceof StaticFormatter sf) {
136                                        current = sf;
137                                }
138                                else if (current != null && f instanceof StaticFormatter sf) {
139                                        current = current.concat(sf);
140                                }
141                                else if (current != null) {
142                                        resolved.add(current);
143                                        resolved.add(f);
144                                        current = null;
145                                }
146                                else {
147                                        resolved.add(f);
148                                }
149                        }
150                        if (current != null) {
151                                resolved.add(current);
152                        }
153                        return resolved.toArray(new LogFormatter[] {});
154                }
155
156                @Override
157                public String toString() {
158                        return "STATIC['" + content + "']";
159                }
160        }
161
162        /**
163         * Controls how a <code>null</code> key value is written by key values formatters, see
164         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder#nullStrategy(KeyValueNullStrategy)}.
165         * The examples below are the default percent encoding; other formats write the same
166         * choices in their own syntax.
167         * <p>
168         * A selected key is treated identically whether it is missing from the
169         * {@link KeyValues} entirely or present but mapped to <code>null</code> -
170         * {@link KeyValues#getValueOrNull(String)} cannot tell those two cases apart, so
171         * neither can this.
172         */
173        @CaseChanging
174        public enum KeyValueNullStrategy {
175
176                /**
177                 * The key is omitted entirely (no key, no <code>=</code>) if its value is
178                 * <code>null</code>.
179                 */
180                SKIP,
181                /**
182                 * A <code>null</code> value is normalized to an empty string, so the key is
183                 * always printed as <code>key=</code> (with nothing after the <code>=</code>)
184                 * regardless of whether the underlying value was <code>null</code> or actually an
185                 * empty string.
186                 */
187                EMPTY,
188                /**
189                 * The <code>null</code>/empty-string distinction is preserved: a
190                 * <code>null</code> value prints just the key with no <code>=</code>, while an
191                 * empty string prints <code>key=</code>. The default; most key values (e.g. MDC)
192                 * are never actually mapped to <code>null</code> in practice, so {@link #SKIP}
193                 * and {@link #KEEP} behave identically until they are.
194                 */
195                KEEP;
196
197        }
198
199        /**
200         * Log formatter builder that is composed of other formatters. The
201         * {@link #add(LogFormatter)} are executed in insertion order. <strong> This builder
202         * is smart and will coalesce and consolidate formatters! </strong> For example if
203         * only formatter is added to the builder it will be returned instead of a new
204         * formatter.
205         */
206        public final static class Builder {
207
208                private List<LogFormatter> formatters = new ArrayList<>();
209
210                private Builder() {
211                }
212
213                /**
214                 * Adds a formatter.
215                 * @param formatter formatter to be added the list of formatters.
216                 * @return this builder.
217                 */
218                public Builder add(LogFormatter formatter) {
219                        formatters.add(formatter);
220                        return this;
221                }
222
223                /**
224                 * Adds an event formatter.
225                 * @param formatter event formatter to be added the list of formatters.
226                 * @return this builder.
227                 */
228                public Builder event(LogFormatter.EventFormatter formatter) {
229                        formatters.add(formatter);
230                        return this;
231                }
232
233                /**
234                 * Append the timestamp in ISO format.
235                 * @return this builder.
236                 */
237                public Builder timeStamp() {
238                        formatters.add(DefaultInstantFormatter.ISO);
239                        return this;
240                }
241
242                /**
243                 * Formatter for {@link LogEvent#timestamp()} derived from standard
244                 * {@link DateTimeFormatter}.
245                 * @param dateTimeFormatter formatter for {@link LogEvent#timestamp()}
246                 * @return this builder.
247                 */
248                public Builder timeStamp(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter) {
249                        formatters.add(TimestampFormatter.of(dateTimeFormatter));
250                        return this;
251                }
252
253                /**
254                 * Adds the default level formatter.
255                 * @return this builder.
256                 * @see LevelFormatter
257                 */
258                public Builder level() {
259                        formatters.add(LogFormatter.LevelFormatter.of());
260                        return this;
261                }
262
263                /**
264                 * Adds the default logger name formatter.
265                 * @return this builder.
266                 */
267                public Builder loggerName() {
268                        formatters.add(DefaultNameFormatter.LOGGER_NAME_FORMATTER);
269                        return this;
270                }
271
272                /**
273                 * Formats the message by calling
274                 * {@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)}.
275                 * @return this builder.
276                 */
277                public Builder message() {
278                        formatters.add(DefaultMessageFormatter.MESSAGE_FORMATTER);
279                        return this;
280                }
281
282                /**
283                 * Appends static text.
284                 * @param content static text.
285                 * @return this builder.
286                 * @see StaticFormatter
287                 */
288                public Builder text(String content) {
289                        formatters.add(new StaticFormatter(content));
290                        return this;
291                }
292
293                /**
294                 * Creates a formatter that will print a single key's value, Logback/Log4j2
295                 * <code>%X{key}</code> style: just the raw value (or the fallback, or an empty
296                 * string if neither is present) - no key prefix, no percent encoding. For the
297                 * percent-encoded <code>key=value</code> style instead, see
298                 * {@link #encodedKeyValue(String, String)}.
299                 * @param key key to select.
300                 * @param fallback if the value is null the fallback will be used.
301                 * @return this.
302                 */
303                public Builder keyValue(String key, @Nullable String fallback) {
304                        return add(new LogbackSingleKeyValueFormatter(key, fallback));
305                }
306
307                /**
308                 * Adds all of the event's key values in the default key values format, percent
309                 * encoded like a URI query: <code>requestId=42&amp;user=Ada%20Lovelace</code>. A
310                 * key mapped to <code>null</code> is written alone, without <code>=</code>. This
311                 * is {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder} with its
312                 * defaults; use {@link #keyValues(Consumer)} for another format, a selection of
313                 * keys, or other null handling.
314                 * @return this.
315                 */
316                public Builder keyValues() {
317                        return add(new KeyValuesFormatterBuilder().build());
318                }
319
320                /**
321                 * Adds the event's key values as configured on a
322                 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder}, which sets the
323                 * format (percent encoding by default, JSON, JSON5, or logfmt), the keys, and the
324                 * null handling, for example:
325                 * {@snippet :
326                 * LogFormatter.builder()
327                 *      .keyValues(kv -> kv.format(KeyValuesFormatterBuilder.Format.LOGFMT).keys(List.of("requestId", "user")));
328                 * }
329                 * @param consumer configures the key values formatter.
330                 * @return this.
331                 */
332                public Builder keyValues(Consumer<KeyValuesFormatterBuilder> consumer) {
333                        var builder = new KeyValuesFormatterBuilder();
334                        consumer.accept(builder);
335                        return add(builder.build());
336                }
337
338                /**
339                 * Creates a formatter that will print a single key value in percent encoding (RFC
340                 * 3986 URI aka the format usually used in {@link URI#getQuery()}). For Logback/
341                 * Log4j2's <code>%X{key}</code> style instead, see
342                 * {@link #keyValue(String, String)}.
343                 * @param key key to select.
344                 * @param fallback if the value is null the fallback will be used.
345                 * @return this.
346                 */
347                public Builder encodedKeyValue(String key, @Nullable String fallback) {
348                        return add(new SingleKeyValueFormatter(key, fallback));
349                }
350
351                /**
352                 * Appends a space.
353                 * @return this builder.
354                 */
355                public Builder space() {
356                        formatters.add(new StaticFormatter(" "));
357                        return this;
358                }
359
360                /**
361                 * Appends text if throwable is set.
362                 * @param text to append if the throwable is set.
363                 * @return this builder.
364                 */
365                public Builder textIfThrowable(String text) {
366                        formatters.add(of((b, e) -> {
367                                if (e.throwableOrNull() != null) {
368                                        b.append(text);
369                                }
370                        }));
371                        return this;
372                }
373
374                /**
375                 * Appends a newline using the platforms line separator.
376                 * @return this builder.
377                 */
378                public Builder newline() {
379                        text(System.lineSeparator());
380                        return this;
381                }
382
383                /**
384                 * Appends a thread name : {@link Thread#getName()}.
385                 * @return this builder.
386                 */
387                public Builder threadName() {
388                        formatters.add(DefaultThreadFormatter.THREAD_NAME_FORMATTER);
389                        return this;
390                }
391
392                /**
393                 * Appends a thread ID : {@link Thread#threadId()}.
394                 * @return this builder.
395                 */
396                public Builder threadId() {
397                        formatters.add(DefaultThreadFormatter.THREAD_ID_FORMATTER);
398                        return this;
399                }
400
401                /**
402                 * Appends the events throwable stack trace.
403                 * @return this.
404                 */
405                public Builder throwable() {
406                        formatters.add(ThrowableFormatter.of());
407                        return this;
408                }
409
410                /**
411                 * Appends the events throwable stack trace using a custom
412                 * {@link ThrowableFormatter} (e.g. one created with
413                 * {@link ThrowableFormatter#builder()}).
414                 * @param throwableFormatter formatter to use.
415                 * @return this.
416                 */
417                public Builder throwable(ThrowableFormatter throwableFormatter) {
418                        formatters.add(throwableFormatter);
419                        return this;
420                }
421
422                /**
423                 * Will create a generic log formatter that has the inner formatters coalesced if
424                 * possible and will noop if there are no formatters.
425                 * @return flattened formatter.
426                 */
427                public LogFormatter build() {
428                        var array = StaticFormatter.coalesce(formatters);
429                        if (array.length == 0) {
430                                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE;
431                        }
432                        if (array.length == 1) {
433                                return array[0];
434                        }
435                        return EventFormatter.of(formatters);
436                }
437
438                /**
439                 * Creates the formatter and starts an encoder builder from it - call
440                 * {@link LogEncoder.Builder#build()} to finish, optionally configuring charset,
441                 * content type, max buffer size, or initial buffer size first.
442                 * @return encoder builder.
443                 * @apiNote for ergonomics
444                 */
445                public LogEncoder.Builder encoder() {
446                        return LogEncoder.builder(build());
447                }
448
449        }
450
451        /**
452         * Generic event formatting that is lambda friendly.
453         */
454        @FunctionalInterface
455        public non-sealed interface EventFormatter extends LogFormatter {
456
457                @Override
458                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event);
459
460                private static EventFormatter of(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
461                        return new CompositeFormatter(StaticFormatter.coalesce(formatters));
462                }
463
464        }
465
466        /**
467         * Formats a {@link Level}.
468         */
469        public sealed interface LevelFormatter extends LogFormatter {
470
471                /**
472                 * Formats the level.
473                 * @param output buffer.
474                 * @param level level.
475                 */
476                void formatLevel(StringBuilder output, Level level);
477
478                @Override
479                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
480                        formatLevel(output, event.level());
481                }
482
483                /**
484                 * Formats a level.
485                 * @param level level
486                 * @return formatted level as a string.
487                 */
488                default String formatLevel(Level level) {
489                        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
490                        formatLevel(sb, level);
491                        return sb.toString();
492                }
493
494                /**
495                 * Default implementation calls {@link LevelFormatter#toString(Level)}
496                 * @return formatter.
497                 */
498                public static LevelFormatter of() {
499                        return DefaultLevelFormatter.LEVEL_FORMATTER;
500                }
501
502                /**
503                 * Default implementation calls {@link LevelFormatter#rightPadded(Level)}
504                 * @return formatter.
505                 */
506                public static LevelFormatter ofRightPadded() {
507                        return DefaultLevelFormatter.RIGHT_PAD_LEVEL_FORMATTER;
508                }
509
510                /**
511                 * Turns a Level into a SLF4J like level String that is all upper case.
512                 * {@link Level#ALL} is "<code>TRACE</code>", {@link Level#OFF} is
513                 * "<code>ERROR</code>" and {@link Level#WARNING} is "<code>WARN</code>".
514                 * @param level system logger level.
515                 * @return upper case string of level.
516                 */
517                public static String toString(Level level) {
518                        return switch (level) {
519                                case DEBUG -> "DEBUG";
520                                case ALL -> "TRACE";
521                                case ERROR -> "ERROR";
522                                case INFO -> "INFO";
523                                case OFF -> "ERROR";
524                                case TRACE -> "TRACE";
525                                case WARNING -> "WARN";
526                        };
527                }
528
529                /**
530                 * Turns a Level into a SLF4J like level String that is all upper case and same
531                 * length with right padding. {@link Level#ALL} is "<code>TRACE</code>",
532                 * {@link Level#OFF} is "<code>ERROR</code>" and {@link Level#WARNING} is
533                 * "<code>WARN</code>".
534                 * @param level system logger level.
535                 * @return upper case string of level.
536                 */
537                public static String rightPadded(Level level) {
538                        return switch (level) {
539                                case DEBUG -> /*   */ "DEBUG";
540                                case ALL -> /*     */ "TRACE";
541                                case ERROR -> /*   */ "ERROR";
542                                case INFO -> /*    */ "INFO ";
543                                case OFF -> /*     */ "ERROR";
544                                case TRACE -> /*   */ "TRACE";
545                                case WARNING -> /* */ "WARN ";
546                        };
547                }
548
549        }
550
551        /**
552         * Formats event timestamps.
553         */
554        public sealed interface TimestampFormatter extends LogFormatter {
555
556                /**
557                 * The default timestamp format used in many logging frameworks which does not
558                 * have dates and only time at millisecond precision.
559                 * <p>
560                 * It is called TTLL as that is the name of the format where it is used in
561                 * logback, log4j etc.
562                 */
563                public static String TTLL_TIME_FORMAT = "HH:mm:ss.SSS";
564
565                /**
566                 * Format timestamp.
567                 * @param output buffer.
568                 * @param instant timestamp.
569                 */
570                void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant);
571
572                @Override
573                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
574                        formatTimestamp(output, event.timestamp());
575                }
576
577                /**
578                 * Formats timestamp using {@link #TTLL_TIME_FORMAT}.
579                 * @return formatter.
580                 */
581                public static TimestampFormatter of() {
582                        return DefaultInstantFormatter.TTLL;
583                }
584
585                /**
586                 * Formats a timestamp using ISO format at fixed millisecond precision (e.g.
587                 * {@code 2023-11-14T22:13:20.123Z}, always exactly 3 fractional digits). Pair
588                 * with {@link #ofMicros()} to append additional sub-millisecond digits, similar
589                 * to Logback's {@code %d{ISO8601}%microsecond}.
590                 * @return formatter.
591                 */
592                public static TimestampFormatter ofISO() {
593                        return DefaultInstantFormatter.ISO;
594                }
595
596                /**
597                 * Micro seconds over the events last second. This is for logback compatibility.
598                 * @return microseconds zero padded.
599                 */
600                public static TimestampFormatter ofMicros() {
601                        return MicrosInstantFormatter.INSTANCE;
602                }
603
604                /**
605                 * Formats a timestamp using standard JDK date time formatter.
606                 * @param dateTimeFormatter date time formatter.
607                 * @return timestamp formatter.
608                 */
609                public static TimestampFormatter of(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter) {
610                        return of(dateTimeFormatter, false);
611                }
612
613                /**
614                 * Formats a timestamp using standard JDK date time formatter.
615                 * <p>
616                 * Formatting with {@link DateTimeFormatter} is comparatively expensive to do on
617                 * every event, so if the caller knows the formatter's finest resolution is
618                 * milliseconds (e.g. a pattern using at most {@code SSS}, never
619                 * {@code n}/{@code N} nanosecond fields), {@code cacheMillisecondPrecision} can
620                 * be set to {@code true} to reuse the previously formatted string whenever
621                 * consecutive events land in the same millisecond - the same trick Logback's
622                 * {@code CachingDateFormatter} and Log4j2's {@code FixedDateFormat} use. Passing
623                 * {@code true} for a formatter that can actually render sub-millisecond precision
624                 * will silently truncate that precision, so only pass {@code true} when the
625                 * pattern is known to not exceed millisecond resolution.
626                 * @param dateTimeFormatter date time formatter.
627                 * @param cacheMillisecondPrecision {@code true} if the formatter's output is
628                 * fully determined by the instant's millisecond value.
629                 * @return timestamp formatter.
630                 */
631                public static TimestampFormatter of(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter, boolean cacheMillisecondPrecision) {
632                        return new DateTimeFormatterInstantFormatter(dateTimeFormatter, cacheMillisecondPrecision);
633                }
634
635        }
636
637        /**
638         * Formats a throwable.
639         */
640        public non-sealed interface ThrowableFormatter extends LogFormatter {
641
642                /**
643                 * Formats a throwable and appends.
644                 * @param output buffer.
645                 * @param throwable throwable.
646                 */
647                void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable);
648
649                @Override
650                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
651                        var t = event.throwableOrNull();
652                        if (t != null) {
653                                formatThrowable(output, t);
654                        }
655                }
656
657                /**
658                 * Default implementation uses {@link Throwable#printStackTrace(PrintWriter)}.
659                 * This formatter is equivalent to {@code of(Integer.MAX_VALUE, List.of())} except
660                 * that it defers entirely to {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} and thus will
661                 * respect any override of that method a particular {@link Throwable} subclass
662                 * might have.
663                 * @return formatter.
664                 */
665                public static ThrowableFormatter of() {
666                        return DefaultThrowableFormatter.INSTANT;
667                }
668
669                /**
670                 * Creates a builder for a throwable formatter that can limit the number of stack
671                 * frame lines shown for each throwable in the cause/suppressed chain, exclude
672                 * frames matching regular expressions, and append packaging data. The output is
673                 * otherwise formatted like {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()}: common frames
674                 * shared with the enclosing throwable are elided the same way (e.g.
675                 * <code>"... 6 more"</code>) as long as the depth limit was not what stopped
676                 * printing; if the depth limit is what stopped printing a
677                 * <code>"... N frames truncated"</code> line is emitted instead.
678                 * @return builder.
679                 * @apiNote a builder left at its defaults (no max lines, exclusions, or packaging
680                 * data) builds {@link #of()} itself; otherwise the built formatter walks
681                 * {@link Throwable#getCause()}/{@link Throwable#getSuppressed()}/
682                 * {@link Throwable#getStackTrace()} directly instead of calling
683                 * {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} and thus will not honor a custom override
684                 * of that method.
685                 */
686                public static Builder builder() {
687                        return new Builder();
688                }
689
690                /**
691                 * Convenience to append a throwable to string builder.
692                 * @param b buffer.
693                 * @param t throwable.
694                 * @apiNote this call creates garbage.
695                 */
696                public static void appendThrowable(StringBuilder b, Throwable t) {
697                        /*
698                         * TODO optimize
699                         */
700                        t.printStackTrace(Internal.StringBuilderPrintWriter.of(b));
701                }
702
703                /**
704                 * Builds a configurable {@link ThrowableFormatter}.
705                 *
706                 * @see ThrowableFormatter#builder()
707                 */
708                public final class Builder {
709
710                        private int maxLines = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
711
712                        private List<String> excludes = List.of();
713
714                        private boolean packagingData = false;
715
716                        private boolean rootCauseFirst = false;
717
718                        private Builder() {
719                        }
720
721                        /**
722                         * Maximum number of stack frame ("at ...") lines printed per throwable in the
723                         * chain. Use {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} for no limit (the default, and matches
724                         * {@link ThrowableFormatter#of()} for well behaved throwables). {@code 0}
725                         * prints just the throwable header lines (class and message) for the whole
726                         * chain with no frames at all.
727                         * @param maxLines maximum stack frame lines per throwable.
728                         * @return this builder.
729                         */
730                        public Builder maxLines(int maxLines) {
731                                this.maxLines = maxLines;
732                                return this;
733                        }
734
735                        /**
736                         * Regular expressions matched with {@link Matcher#find()} against each
737                         * frame's {@link StackTraceElement#toString()}. A frame matching any of these
738                         * is omitted entirely and does not count against {@link #maxLines(int)}.
739                         * Defaults to empty (no filtering).
740                         * @param excludes exclude patterns.
741                         * @return this builder.
742                         */
743                        public Builder excludes(List<String> excludes) {
744                                this.excludes = excludes;
745                                return this;
746                        }
747
748                        /**
749                         * Whether to append packaging data (the jar or module a frame's class was
750                         * loaded from, and its version) after each frame line, e.g.
751                         * <code>[myapp-1.0.jar:1.0]</code> or <code>[java.base:na]</code>. This
752                         * mirrors (but does not byte-for-byte match) logback's
753                         * <code>ExtendedThrowableProxyConverter</code> output. Resolution requires
754                         * loading the frame's class (without initializing it) and can fail silently
755                         * to <code>[na:na]</code> for frames whose class cannot be loaded (e.g.
756                         * dynamically generated classes). This has a real per-frame cost so it
757                         * defaults to <code>false</code>.
758                         * @param packagingData true to append packaging data.
759                         * @return this builder.
760                         */
761                        public Builder packagingData(boolean packagingData) {
762                                this.packagingData = packagingData;
763                                return this;
764                        }
765
766                        /**
767                         * Whether to print the root cause first instead of last, working back up
768                         * through each wrapping exception ("Wrapped by: ..." instead of "Caused by:
769                         * ..."), mirroring logback's
770                         * <code>RootCauseFirstThrowableProxyConverter</code> (<code>%rEx</code>/
771                         * <code>%rootException</code>). Frame trimming (common-frame elision against
772                         * each throwable's own wrapper, {@link #maxLines(int)},
773                         * {@link #excludes(List)}) behaves identically either way - only the print
774                         * order and the "Caused by:"/"Wrapped by:" captions differ. Defaults to
775                         * <code>false</code>.
776                         * @param rootCauseFirst true to print the root cause first.
777                         * @return this builder.
778                         */
779                        public Builder rootCauseFirst(boolean rootCauseFirst) {
780                                this.rootCauseFirst = rootCauseFirst;
781                                return this;
782                        }
783
784                        /**
785                         * Builds the formatter. If none of {@link #maxLines(int)},
786                         * {@link #excludes(List)}, {@link #packagingData(boolean)}, or
787                         * {@link #rootCauseFirst(boolean)} were set away from their defaults, returns
788                         * {@link ThrowableFormatter#of()} (i.e. plain
789                         * {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} behavior) instead of constructing a
790                         * formatter that walks the throwable manually for no reason.
791                         * @return formatter.
792                         */
793                        public ThrowableFormatter build() {
794                                if (maxLines == Integer.MAX_VALUE && excludes.isEmpty() && !packagingData && !rootCauseFirst) {
795                                        return ThrowableFormatter.of();
796                                }
797                                List<Pattern> compiled = excludes.isEmpty() ? List.of()
798                                                : excludes.stream().map(Pattern::compile).toList();
799                                var resolver = packagingData ? new PackagingDataResolver() : null;
800                                var framePrinter = new ThrowableFramePrinter(maxLines, compiled, resolver);
801                                if (rootCauseFirst) {
802                                        return new RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter(framePrinter);
803                                }
804                                return new StandardThrowableFormatter(framePrinter);
805                        }
806
807                }
808
809        }
810
811        /**
812         * Tests if the log formatter is noop or is null which will be considered as noop.
813         * @param logFormatter formatter which <strong>can be <code>null</code></strong>!
814         * @return true if the formatter should not be used.
815         */
816        public static boolean isNoopOrNull(@Nullable LogFormatter logFormatter) {
817                return logFormatter == null || logFormatter.isNoop();
818        }
819
820        /**
821         * Pads the right hand side of text with space.
822         * @param sb buffer.
823         * @param s string that will be appended first (left hand) and will not be longer than
824         * the <code>n</code> parameter.
825         * @param n the size of string. If the size is bigger than passed in string the result
826         * will have padding otherwise the passed in string will be cut to the size of this
827         * parameter.
828         */
829        public static void padRight(StringBuilder sb, CharSequence s, int n) {
830                int length = s.length();
831                if (length >= n) {
832                        sb.append(s, 0, n);
833                        return;
834                }
835                sb.append(s);
836                spacePad(sb, n - length);
837        }
838
839        /**
840         * Pads the left hand side of text with space.
841         * @param sb buffer.
842         * @param s string that will be appended second (right hand) and will not be longer
843         * than the <code>n</code> parameter.
844         * @param n the size of string. If the size is bigger than passed in string the result
845         * will have padding otherwise the passed in string will be cut to the size of this
846         * parameter.
847         */
848        public static void padLeft(StringBuilder sb, CharSequence s, int n) {
849                int length = s.length();
850                if (length >= n) {
851                        sb.append(s, 0, n);
852                        return;
853                }
854                spacePad(sb, n - length);
855                sb.append(s);
856        }
857
858        /**
859         * Fast space padding method.
860         */
861        private static void spacePad(final StringBuilder sbuf, final int length) {
862                int l = length;
863                while (l >= 32) {
864                        sbuf.append(CompositeFormatter.SPACES[5]);
865                        l -= 32;
866                }
867
868                for (int i = 4; i >= 0; i--) {
869                        if ((l & (1 << i)) != 0) {
870                                sbuf.append(CompositeFormatter.SPACES[i]);
871                        }
872                }
873        }
874
875        /**
876         * A special formatter that will do nothing.
877         */
878        enum NoopFormatter implements TimestampFormatter, ThrowableFormatter, LevelFormatter {
879
880                /**
881                 * instance.
882                 */
883                INSTANCE;
884
885                @Override
886                public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
887                }
888
889                @Override
890                public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
891                }
892
893                @Override
894                public void formatLevel(StringBuilder output, Level level) {
895                }
896
897                @Override
898                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
899                }
900
901        }
902
903}

905@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent")
906record CompositeFormatter(LogFormatter[] formatters) implements EventFormatter {
907
908        static String[] SPACES = { " ", "  ", "    ", "        ", // 1,2,4,8 spaces
909                        "                ", // 16 spaces
910                        "                                " }; // 32 spaces
911
912        @Override
913        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
914                for (var formatter : formatters) {
915                        formatter.format(output, event);
916                }
917        }
918
919        @Override
920        public String toString() {
921                return getClass().getSimpleName() + Arrays.toString(formatters);
922        }
923
924        public static List<LogFormatter> flatten(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
925                return List.copyOf(_flatten(formatters));
926        }
927
928        private static List<LogFormatter> _flatten(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
929                List<LogFormatter> result = new ArrayList<>();
930                for (var f : formatters) {
931                        if (f instanceof CompositeFormatter cf) {
932                                result.addAll(_flatten(cf));
933                        }
934                        else {
935                                result.add(f);
936                        }
937                }
938                return result;
939        }
940
941        private static List<LogFormatter> _flatten(CompositeFormatter formatter) {
942                var formatters = formatter.formatters;
943                return _flatten(Arrays.asList(formatters));
944        }
945
946}

1006/**
1007 * Not an enum: error-prone's immutable-enum check flags enums holding mutable state, and
1008 * {@link #cache} is mutable (an {@link java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference}).
1009 * {@link #description} exists solely to give each instance a stable identity for
1010 * {@link #toString()}.
1011 */
1012final class DefaultInstantFormatter implements TimestampFormatter {
1013
1014        static final DefaultInstantFormatter TTLL = new DefaultInstantFormatter("TTLL",
1015                        DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(TTLL_TIME_FORMAT).withZone(ZoneId.from(ZoneOffset.UTC)));
1016
1017        /*
1018         * appendInstant(3) renders a fixed-width 3-digit millisecond fraction (unlike
1019         * DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME, which renders a variable-width fraction of 0-9
1020         * digits based on the instant's actual sub-millisecond value) - fixed width matches
1021         * Logback/Log4j2's ISO output and is what makes this safe to millis-cache.
1022         */
1023        static final DefaultInstantFormatter ISO = new DefaultInstantFormatter("ISO",
1024                        new DateTimeFormatterBuilder().appendInstant(3).toFormatter());
1025
1026        private final String description;
1027
1028        private final DateTimeFormatter formatter;
1029
1030        private final MillisCache cache = new MillisCache();
1031
1032        private DefaultInstantFormatter(String description, DateTimeFormatter formatter) {
1033                this.description = description;
1034                this.formatter = formatter;
1035        }
1036
1037        @Override
1038        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
1039                cache.formatTimestamp(output, instant, formatter);
1040        }
1041
1042        @Override
1043        public String toString() {
1044                return description;
1045        }

1049/**
1050 * Micro seconds over the events last second, for Logback compatibility - meant to be
1051 * composed after a millisecond-precision timestamp (see
1052 * {@link TimestampFormatter#ofISO()}). Stateless, so a singleton enum works cleanly here
1053 * (unlike {@link DefaultInstantFormatter}, nothing here trips error-prone's
1054 * immutable-enum check).
1055 */
1056enum MicrosInstantFormatter implements TimestampFormatter {
1057
1058        INSTANCE;
1059
1060        @Override
1061        @SuppressWarnings("JavaInstantGetSecondsGetNano")
1062        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
1063                int nanos = instant.getNano();
1064
1065                int millis_and_micros = nanos / 1000;
1066                int micros = millis_and_micros % 1000;
1067
1068                if (micros >= 100) {
1069                        output.append(micros);
1070                }
1071                else if (micros >= 10) {
1072                        output.append("0").append(micros);
1073                }
1074                else {
1075                        output.append("00").append(micros);
1076                }
1077        }
1078
1079}

1081final class DateTimeFormatterInstantFormatter implements TimestampFormatter {

1090        }

1094                var c = cache;
1095                if (c == null) {
1096                        dateTimeFormatter.formatTo(instant, output);
1097                        return;
1098                }
1099                c.formatTimestamp(output, instant, dateTimeFormatter);

1104/**
1105 * Caches a formatted timestamp string keyed by the instant's millisecond value, the same
1106 * trick Logback's {@code CachingDateFormatter} and Log4j2's {@code FixedDateFormat} use -
1107 * reformatting only happens when consecutive events land in different milliseconds. Only
1108 * correct for formatters whose output is fully determined by millisecond precision
1109 * (callers are responsible for that guarantee).
1110 */
1111final class MillisCache {
1112
1113        private record Entry(long millis, String formatted) {
1114        }
1115
1116        private static final Entry EMPTY = new Entry(Long.MIN_VALUE, "");
1117
1118        private final AtomicReference<Entry> ref = new AtomicReference<>(EMPTY);
1119
1120        void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant, DateTimeFormatter formatter) {
1121                long millis = instant.toEpochMilli();
1122                Entry cached = ref.get();
1123                if (cached.millis() == millis) {
1124                        output.append(cached.formatted());
1125                        return;
1126                }
1127                StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(32);
1128                formatter.formatTo(instant, sb);
1129                String formatted = sb.toString();
1130                ref.set(new Entry(millis, formatted));
1131                output.append(formatted);
1132        }
1133
1134}

1147/**
1148 * Prints stack frames trimmed by {@link Builder#maxLines(int) maxLines}/
1149 * {@link Builder#excludes(List) excludes} and optionally appended with packaging data -
1150 * shared as-is between {@link StandardThrowableFormatter} and
1151 * {@link RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter}, which differ only in traversal order and
1152 * caption choice, never in how an individual throwable's own frames get printed.
1153 */
1154final class ThrowableFramePrinter {
1155
1156        private final int maxLines;
1157
1158        private final List<Pattern> excludes;
1159
1160        private final @Nullable PackagingDataResolver packagingData;
1161
1162        ThrowableFramePrinter(int maxLines, List<Pattern> excludes, @Nullable PackagingDataResolver packagingData) {
1163                this.maxLines = maxLines;
1164                this.excludes = excludes;
1165                this.packagingData = packagingData;
1166        }
1167
1168        /*
1169         * Prints trace's frames, trimmed against enclosingTrace's shared trailing frames (a
1170         * throwable typically shares a stack-trace suffix with whatever holds it as its
1171         * cause, from how the JVM captures traces at throw time) the same way
1172         * Throwable#printStackTrace() does - "... N more" if elision fully accounts for the
1173         * missing frames, nothing if maxLines/excludes already cut the visible output short
1174         * first. Shared verbatim by StandardThrowableFormatter (enclosingTrace = the trace of
1175         * whatever this throwable is the cause of) and RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter
1176         * (enclosingTrace = the same relationship, just discovered while recursing the other
1177         * direction) - the "which throwable wraps which" relationship this depends on does
1178         * not change with print order.
1179         */
1180        void printFramesAgainstEnclosing(StringBuilder output, StackTraceElement[] trace,
1181                        StackTraceElement[] enclosingTrace, String prefix) {
1182                int m = trace.length - 1;
1183                int n = enclosingTrace.length - 1;
1184                while (m >= 0 && n >= 0 && trace[m].equals(enclosingTrace[n])) {
1185                        m--;
1186                        n--;
1187                }
1188                int framesInCommon = trace.length - 1 - m;
1189                boolean truncated = printFrames(output, trace, m + 1, prefix);
1190                if (!truncated && framesInCommon > 0) {
1191                        output.append(prefix)
1192                                .append("\t... ")
1193                                .append(framesInCommon)
1194                                .append(" more")
1195                                .append(System.lineSeparator());
1196                }
1197        }
1198
1199        /*
1200         * Prints frames trace[0..count) filtered by excludes and capped at maxLines. Returns
1201         * true if there were excluded-filtered frames beyond maxLines (i.e. the output was
1202         * cut short because of maxLines rather than ending naturally).
1203         */
1204        boolean printFrames(StringBuilder output, StackTraceElement[] trace, int count, String prefix) {
1205                int printed = 0;
1206                int available = 0;
1207                for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
1208                        var element = trace[i];
1209                        if (isExcluded(element)) {
1210                                continue;
1211                        }
1212                        available++;
1213                        if (printed < maxLines) {
1214                                output.append(prefix).append("\tat ").append(element);
1215                                // Eclipse null analysis is too dumb about final fields.
1216                                var packagingData = this.packagingData;
1217                                if (packagingData != null) {
1218                                        output.append(' ').append(packagingData.resolve(element));
1219                                }
1220                                output.append(System.lineSeparator());
1221                                printed++;
1222                        }
1223                }
1224                if (available > maxLines) {
1225                        output.append(prefix)
1226                                .append("\t... ")
1227                                .append(available - maxLines)
1228                                .append(" frames truncated")
1229                                .append(System.lineSeparator());
1230                        return true;
1231                }
1232                return false;
1233        }
1234
1235        private boolean isExcluded(StackTraceElement element) {
1236                if (excludes.isEmpty()) {
1237                        return false;
1238                }
1239                String s = element.toString();
1240                for (var p : excludes) {
1241                        Matcher matcher = p.matcher(s);
1242                        if (matcher.find()) {
1243                                return true;
1244                        }
1245                }
1246                return false;
1247        }
1248
1249}
1250
1251/**
1252 * Reimplements {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()}'s algorithm (header line, frames,
1253 * common-frame elision against the enclosing trace, "Caused by:"/"Suppressed:" sections,
1254 * circular reference guard) so that a max line count and frame exclusion patterns can be
1255 * applied while printing.
1256 */
1257final class StandardThrowableFormatter implements ThrowableFormatter {
1258
1259        private static final String CAUSE_CAPTION = "Caused by: ";
1260
1261        private static final String SUPPRESSED_CAPTION = "Suppressed: ";
1262
1263        private final ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter;
1264
1265        StandardThrowableFormatter(ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter) {
1266                this.framePrinter = framePrinter;
1267        }
1268
1269        @Override
1270        public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
1271                Set<Throwable> dejaVu = Collections.newSetFromMap(new IdentityHashMap<>());
1272                dejaVu.add(throwable);
1273                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1274                output.append(throwable).append(System.lineSeparator());
1275                framePrinter.printFrames(output, trace, trace.length, "");
1276                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1277                        printEnclosed(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, "\t", dejaVu);
1278                }
1279                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1280                if (cause != null) {
1281                        printEnclosed(output, cause, trace, CAUSE_CAPTION, "", dejaVu);
1282                }
1283        }
1284
1285        private void printEnclosed(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable, StackTraceElement[] enclosingTrace,
1286                        String caption, String prefix, Set<Throwable> dejaVu) {
1287                if (!dejaVu.add(throwable)) {
1288                        output.append(prefix)
1289                                .append("[CIRCULAR REFERENCE: ")
1290                                .append(throwable)
1291                                .append(']')
1292                                .append(System.lineSeparator());
1293                        return;
1294                }
1295                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1296                output.append(prefix).append(caption).append(throwable).append(System.lineSeparator());
1297                framePrinter.printFramesAgainstEnclosing(output, trace, enclosingTrace, prefix);
1298                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1299                        printEnclosed(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, prefix + "\t", dejaVu);
1300                }
1301                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1302                if (cause != null) {
1303                        printEnclosed(output, cause, trace, CAUSE_CAPTION, prefix, dejaVu);
1304                }
1305        }
1306
1307}
1308
1309/**
1310 * Mirrors logback's <code>RootCauseFirstThrowableProxyConverter</code>: same frame
1311 * trimming/common-frame elision as {@link StandardThrowableFormatter}, but the root cause
1312 * prints first and each wrapper prints afterward, captioned "Wrapped by: " instead of
1313 * "Caused by: ". Common-frame elision for a given throwable is still computed against its
1314 * own direct wrapper's frames (the throwable that has it as {@link Throwable#getCause()})
1315 * regardless of print order - that relationship, and therefore the elision counts, do not
1316 * depend on which order things are printed in.
1317 * <p>
1318 * A suppressed exception's own "Suppressed: " caption lands on the first line actually
1319 * printed for it - the root of <em>its</em> own cause chain if it has one, not the
1320 * suppressed exception's own header - matching logback's
1321 * <code>recursiveAppendRootCauseFirst</code> exactly (the caption is threaded down
1322 * through the recursion and only consumed once, at the bottom).
1323 */
1324final class RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter implements ThrowableFormatter {
1325
1326        private static final String WRAPPED_BY_CAPTION = "Wrapped by: ";
1327
1328        private static final String SUPPRESSED_CAPTION = "Suppressed: ";
1329
1330        private final ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter;
1331
1332        RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter(ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter) {
1333                this.framePrinter = framePrinter;
1334        }
1335
1336        @Override
1337        public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
1338                Set<Throwable> dejaVu = Collections.newSetFromMap(new IdentityHashMap<>());
1339                print(output, throwable, null, null, "", dejaVu);
1340        }
1341
1342        private void print(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable, StackTraceElement @Nullable [] enclosingTrace,
1343                        @Nullable String caption, String prefix, Set<Throwable> dejaVu) {
1344                if (!dejaVu.add(throwable)) {
1345                        output.append(prefix);
1346                        if (caption != null) {
1347                                output.append(caption);
1348                        }
1349                        output.append("[CIRCULAR REFERENCE: ").append(throwable).append(']').append(System.lineSeparator());
1350                        return;
1351                }
1352                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1353                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1354                if (cause != null) {
1355                        print(output, cause, trace, caption, prefix, dejaVu);
1356                        caption = null; // consumed by the recursive (deeper) call above
1357                }
1358                output.append(prefix);
1359                if (caption != null) {
1360                        output.append(caption);
1361                }
1362                if (cause != null) {
1363                        output.append(WRAPPED_BY_CAPTION);
1364                }
1365                output.append(throwable).append(System.lineSeparator());
1366                if (enclosingTrace == null) {
1367                        framePrinter.printFrames(output, trace, trace.length, prefix);
1368                }
1369                else {
1370                        framePrinter.printFramesAgainstEnclosing(output, trace, enclosingTrace, prefix);
1371                }
1372                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1373                        print(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, prefix + "\t", dejaVu);
1374                }
1375        }
1376
1377}
1378
1379/**
1380 * Resolves and caches which jar/module/directory a stack frame's class was loaded from
1381 * and its reported version, formatted as <code>[location:version]</code>. Named modules
1382 * (including JDK frames) are resolved for free from the frame itself or the loaded
1383 * class's {@link Module} without touching a {@link java.security.CodeSource}. Classpath
1384 * (unnamed module) frames fall back to the class's {@link java.security.CodeSource} and
1385 * {@link Package#getImplementationVersion()}. Either "location" or "version" is
1386 * <code>na</code> when unknown, and the whole result is <code>[na:na]</code> when the
1387 * frame's class cannot be loaded at all (e.g. dynamically generated classes).
1388 */
1389final class PackagingDataResolver {
1390
1391        private final ConcurrentMap<String, String> cache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
1392
1393        String resolve(StackTraceElement element) {
1394                String className = element.getClassName();
1395                String cached = cache.get(className);
1396                if (cached != null) {
1397                        return cached;
1398                }
1399                String computed = compute(element);
1400                cache.put(className, computed);
1401                return computed;
1402        }
1403
1404        private static String compute(StackTraceElement element) {
1405                String moduleName = element.getModuleName();
1406                if (moduleName != null) {
1407                        return format(moduleName, element.getModuleVersion());
1408                }
1409                Class<?> type = load(element.getClassName());
1410                if (type == null) {
1411                        return "[na:na]";
1412                }
1413                Module module = type.getModule();
1414                if (module.isNamed()) {
1415                        var descriptor = module.getDescriptor();
1416                        String version = descriptor == null ? null : descriptor.rawVersion().orElse(null);
1417                        return format(module.getName(), version);
1418                }
1419                var codeSource = type.getProtectionDomain().getCodeSource();
1420                if (codeSource == null) {
1421                        return "[na:na]";
1422                }
1423                var location = codeSource.getLocation();
1424                if (location == null) {
1425                        return "[na:na]";
1426                }
1427                String path = location.getPath();
1428                if (path == null || path.isEmpty()) {
1429                        path = location.toString();
1430                }
1431                if (path.endsWith("/")) {
1432                        path = path.substring(0, path.length() - 1);
1433                }
1434                int slash = path.lastIndexOf('/');
1435                String name = slash >= 0 && slash < path.length() - 1 ? path.substring(slash + 1) : path;
1436                var pkg = type.getPackage();
1437                String version = pkg == null ? null : pkg.getImplementationVersion();
1438                return format(name, version);
1439        }
1440
1441        private static String format(String location, @Nullable String version) {
1442                return "[" + location + ":" + (version == null || version.isEmpty() ? "na" : version) + "]";
1443        }
1444
1445        private static @Nullable Class<?> load(String className) {
1446                var contextLoader = Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader();
1447                if (contextLoader != null) {
1448                        var type = loadOrNull(className, contextLoader);
1449                        if (type != null) {
1450                                return type;
1451                        }
1452                }
1453                return loadOrNull(className, PackagingDataResolver.class.getClassLoader());
1454        }
1455
1456        private static @Nullable Class<?> loadOrNull(String className, @Nullable ClassLoader loader) {
1457                try {
1458                        return Class.forName(className, false, loader);
1459                }
1460                catch (ClassNotFoundException | LinkageError | SecurityException e) {
1461                        return null;
1462                }
1463        }
1464
1465}
1466
1467record SingleKeyValueFormatter(String key, @Nullable String fallback) implements LogFormatter {
1468        @Override
1469        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1470                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1471                formatKeyValues(output, kvs);
1472        }
1473
1474        void formatKeyValues(StringBuilder output, KeyValues keyValues) {
1475                String v = keyValues.getValueOrNull(key);
1476                if (v == null) {
1477                        v = fallback;
1478                }
1479                PercentCodec.encode(output, key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1480                if (v != null) {
1481                        output.append('=');
1482                        PercentCodec.encode(output, v, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1483                }
1484        }
1485
1486}
1487
1488/**
1489 * Logback/Log4j2 <code>%X{key}</code> style: just the raw value (or fallback, or empty
1490 * string), no key prefix, no percent encoding. See
1491 * {@link LogFormatter.Builder#keyValue(String, String)}.
1492 */
1493record LogbackSingleKeyValueFormatter(String key, @Nullable String fallback) implements LogFormatter {
1494
1495        @Override
1496        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1497                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1498                String v = kvs.getValueOrNull(key);
1499                if (v == null) {
1500                        v = fallback;
1501                }
1502                if (v != null) {
1503                        output.append(v);
1504                }
1505        }
1506
1507}
